solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Leave home by November to make film

indicators.note: by means next to, so one piece is set alongside the other

blocks.note: leave from work is a holiday
at home means in
N is November in the NATO alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone takes time off and goes home to shoot a movie in November.
explanation.walkthrough: Holiday Inn is the 1942 Bing Crosby film that introduced the song White Christmas.
explanation.definitionFit: The answer is the title of a well-known musical motion picture, so it is an example of the category named.

clue.text: Henry's revolting, pulling down large bloomers

indicators.note: pulling something down moves it lower, so a letter is shifted further down this down entry

blocks.note: Hal is the familiar name of Shakespeare's Prince Henry
's stands for is, and is revolting means rebels
L is the abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: A rebellious Henry is tugging down an outsize pair of knickers.
explanation.walkthrough: Henry's revolting reads as Henry rebels; pulling down moves the letter for large lower in this down entry, to just before the last letter. Bloomers are old-fashioned baggy knickers, but here they are things that bloom.
explanation.definitionFit: Harebells are wild flowers, and a flower is a bloomer in the crossword sense of something that blooms.

clue.text: Giving protection to clubs, enticement for crooked coppers?

indicators.note: to protect something is to wrap around it, so the outer word encloses the other

blocks.note: a lure is an enticement
C is the card-suit abbreviation for clubs

explanation.surface: Bent police officers are tempted by a lure that covers for golf clubs.
explanation.walkthrough: Coppers here are copper coins, not police: filthy lucre is money gained dishonestly.
explanation.definitionFit: Lucre is money, especially ill-gotten, so dishonestly obtained cash fits the question-marked phrase.

clue.text: Police officer seeing shot in the air near corridor in parliament

blocks.note: DI is a Detective Inspector
vision is the faculty of seeing
a lob is a high looping shot
by means near

explanation.surface: A police officer watches someone fire a shot into the air near a Westminster corridor.
explanation.walkthrough: MPs vote in the House of Commons by walking through one of two division lobbies, the Ayes or the Noes.
explanation.definitionFit: A division lobby is one of the corridors beside the Commons chamber that members pass through to record their votes.

clue.text: Branch of police department that supported hangings?

blocks.note: the Yard is Scotland Yard, the Metropolitan Police headquarters
an arm is a branch of an organisation

explanation.surface: A section of the police once took charge of executions.
explanation.walkthrough: Read backwards from the clue: the Yard's arm. Sailors were hanged from the yardarm, the spar end on a ship's mast, and sails hang from it too.
explanation.definitionFit: A yardarm is the outer end of a spar on a mast, from which sails and, notoriously, condemned men were hung.

clue.text: Rather Flo than Dicky

indicators.note: dicky is British slang for faulty or unsound, so the letters are out of order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone would sooner have Flo than Dicky, two people with pet names.
explanation.walkthrough: Dicky looks like a man's name to set beside Flo, but it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Not half is British slang for an emphatic yes, as is Rather! said in reply to a question.

clue.text: Mark clock setting

blocks.note: first meaning: a small stain or blemish
second meaning: to notice, as in British slang to clock someone
third meaning: a place or location

explanation.surface: Someone notes how a clock has been set.
explanation.walkthrough: Three separate meanings rather than two; clock is British slang for notice.
explanation.definitionFit: The short word means a blemish, means to catch sight of, and means a particular place.

clue.text: Letter in Irish supporting sensationalist preacher

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other
in a down entry a supporting piece sits underneath, so it follows the other

blocks.note: pulp fiction is sensationalist writing
IR is an abbreviation for Irish
tee is the spelt-out name of the letter T

explanation.surface: An Irish letter backs a tabloid-style preacher.
explanation.definitionFit: A pulpiteer is a mildly scornful word for a preacher, one who holds forth from the pulpit.

clue.text: City suffering reverse, way too predictable at home

indicators.note: a reverse is a turnaround, so the word is read backwards

blocks.note: a rut is a groove of dull routine
at home means in

explanation.surface: A football club's city side suffers a defeat, too predictable at home.
explanation.definitionFit: Turin is a major city in north-west Italy, capital of Piedmont.

clue.text: Rally in park finished

blocks.note: the rec is a recreation ground, a public park
over means finished

explanation.surface: A protest rally in the park has wrapped up.
explanation.walkthrough: The rec is British shorthand for a recreation ground.
explanation.definitionFit: To rally is to regain strength or health, which is to recover.

clue.text: Supper often late initially stops one rewarding waiter

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word before it
a stopper plugs a gap, so one piece is lodged inside the other

blocks.note: someone who rewards a waiter leaves a tip
the first letter of late

explanation.surface: A diner who often eats late interrupts the person paying the waiter.
explanation.walkthrough: Supper is not the meal but one who sups, that is drinks, and does so often.
explanation.definitionFit: A tippler is a habitual drinker, someone who sups alcohol frequently.

clue.text: Crackpot jailer cut loose for a prank

indicators.note: cutting something shortens it, so the final letter goes
letters set loose are free to fall into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
jailer without its last letter

explanation.surface: A deranged prison guard lets inmates go free as a jape.
explanation.definitionFit: A practical joke is a trick played on someone for amusement, which is what a prank is.

clue.text: Bishop with respect to rabbi has one … to anoint

blocks.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

blocks.clueFragment: with respect to rabbi has one
blocks.note: the word bishop contains a single B and the word rabbi two, so it has one fewer

explanation.surface: A puzzling comparison of bishop and rabbi trails off before a religious anointing.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis is the gap to fill: bishop, compared with rabbi, has one B LESS. The answer completes the sentence as well as meaning anoint.
explanation.definitionFit: To bless is to consecrate with a religious rite, and anointing with oil is such a consecration.

clue.text: A socialist party dictator embracing a US native

indicators.note: to embrace is to hold in the arms, so one piece surrounds the other

blocks.note: taken as written
Lab is the abbreviation for the British Labour Party
Idi Amin was the dictator of Uganda
taken as written

explanation.surface: A left-wing party's strongman holds an American in his grip.
explanation.definitionFit: An Alabamian is a person born in the US state of Alabama.

clue.text: Country anthem having line also belonging to pop

blocks.note: L is the abbreviation for line
and means also
pop is my father, so belonging to him is of my father's

explanation.surface: A national song gets a line borrowed from pop music.
explanation.walkthrough: Pop looks like pop music but is Dad. The answer is the English title of Hen Wlad Fy Nhadau, the national anthem of Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: Land of My Fathers is the national anthem of Wales, so it is the anthem of a particular country.

clue.text: Having no side in rugby to beat upset supporter

indicators.note: in a down entry upset turns the words before it upside down, so they read bottom to top

blocks.note: RU is Rugby Union
to tan someone's hide is to beat them
an ally supports you

explanation.surface: A rugby player with no team to beat is cross with his own backer.
explanation.walkthrough: Side is British for airs and graces: someone with no side has no pretension. The definition is adverbial, describing behaving without side.
explanation.definitionFit: To act naturally is to behave unaffectedly, without airs or pretence, which is having no side.

clue.text: Accessory for stocking freezer

blocks.note: first meaning: a garter strap that holds up a stocking
second meaning: one who halts something, as accounts or play are frozen

explanation.surface: A shop item for stocking a freezer.
explanation.walkthrough: Stocking looks like filling shelves, and freezer like a kitchen appliance; both are other senses.
explanation.definitionFit: A suspender holds up hosiery, and one who suspends an activity halts or freezes it.

clue.text: Get even less to do: secret left to be cracked

indicators.note: something cracked is broken apart, so these letters are rebuilt in a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: Someone wants an easier life, with a secret code still to be cracked.
explanation.definitionFit: To settle old scores is to take revenge for past wrongs, which is to get even.

clue.text: Yellow light round US resort

blocks.note: or is gold or yellow in heraldry
to light on something is to land on it
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: A yellow lamp shines around an American holiday town.
explanation.walkthrough: Light reads as a lamp, but it is the verb meaning to come down or settle.
explanation.definitionFit: Orlando in Florida is the American holiday destination famous for its theme parks.

clue.text: Provide place for retirement or escape

blocks.note: to do a meal is to provide it
a bunk is a bed, where you retire at night

explanation.surface: Somewhere to stay is needed for an old person's retirement, or else a getaway.
explanation.walkthrough: Retirement is going to bed, not leaving work. To do a bunk is British slang for running away.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing a bunk is British slang for leaving in a hurry to avoid something, which is an escape.

clue.text: Wonders if one should intercept airmail book when dispatched

indicators.note: things dispatched are sent off and scattered, so these letters are thrown into a new arrangement

blocks.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
taken as written
B is the abbreviation for book

explanation.surface: Someone muses whether a person should seize a book sent by airmail.
explanation.walkthrough: Wonders looks like a verb, as in muses, but it is a plural noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Mirabilia is a Latin plural meaning marvels or remarkable things.

clue.text: Get away from YHA, travel lodges

indicators.note: something that lodges is housed inside, so the answer sits within the neighbouring words

blocks.note: letters running across from, YHA and travel

explanation.surface: Escape from a youth-hostel trip that stays at lodges.
explanation.walkthrough: The YHA is the Youth Hostels Association. Get away! is an exclamation of disbelief, as is the old-fashioned My hat!
explanation.definitionFit: Both are exclamations of surprise or incredulity, so one interjection can stand in for the other.

clue.text: Crafting tool cutting end off flap

indicators.note: cutting the end off removes the final letter of the word that follows

blocks.note: to be in a lather is to be in a flap

explanation.surface: A craftsman's tool slices the end off a flap of material.
explanation.walkthrough: Flap here is a state of agitation, not a piece of material.
explanation.definitionFit: A lathe is a machine that turns wood or metal so it can be shaped, a tool for crafting.

clue.text: Capable of high speed — or not?

blocks.note: surface reading: describing a fast motorbike or car
setter's reading: in a down entry the word not, written going up, is the answer

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether a vehicle can really go fast.
explanation.walkthrough: NOT written upwards gives TON, followed by UP, so TON-UP describes itself. A ton-up is British slang for 100 mph, especially on a motorbike.
explanation.definitionFit: A ton-up machine or rider reaches a hundred miles an hour, the ton in British slang.

clue.text: Carefree? Not exactly, and note reflected that

indicators.note: a reflection shows things mirror-wise, so the preceding pieces read backwards

blocks.note: c, for circa, means about or approximately
lah is the sixth note of the sol-fa scale
yon is an old word for that

explanation.surface: Someone asks if they are carefree and admits not quite.
explanation.walkthrough: Not exactly looks like a reply to the question, but it is the abbreviation for circa.
explanation.definitionFit: Halcyon days are idyllic and untroubled, so the adjective means calm and free from care.

clue.text: Now, nude dancing is not acknowledged

indicators.note: dancing letters move about and change places

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Naked dancing is now something no one admits to.
explanation.definitionFit: To own something can mean to admit it, so an unowned act is one nobody admits to.

clue.text: Plays etc? Oh yes, every so often

indicators.note: every so often picks letters at regular gaps, here every second one

blocks.note: the even letters of etc oh yes

explanation.surface: Plays and the like? Yes, now and then.
explanation.definitionFit: To toy with something is to play with it idly, so the verb forms are equivalent.

clue.text: Reserve goalie an expert at balancing acts?

blocks.note: to book is to reserve
a goalie is the goalkeeper

explanation.surface: A substitute goalkeeper is skilled at circus balancing acts.
explanation.walkthrough: Reserve looks like a substitute player beside goalie, but it is a verb. Acts is short for accounts.
explanation.definitionFit: A bookkeeper records transactions and balances the accounts of a business.
